title: Keep each LangChain example tool bound to its own callback
prompt:
Change only src/app/docs/guides/langchain-setup/page.tsx among production files. Evidence: src/app/docs/guides/langchain-setup/page.tsx:96-113 creates _call in a loop, then stores synchronous and asynchronous lambdas that resolve the shared _call variable later. Although _call captures tool_name in a default argument, the lambdas do not capture that function. Executing the actual get_bazaar_tools snippet with two stub tools named first and second made both asynchronous wrappers invoke second. A developer copying this adapter can silently execute the wrong tool.

Bind both wrappers to the per-iteration callback, using a small local factory within the displayed Python snippet or an equivalent closure-safe construction. Preserve names, descriptions, argument forwarding, and output serialization. This job fixes callback identity only; do not redesign framework integration, transport setup, billing, or the event-loop policy.

Add exactly one new test file, tests/langchain-tool-closure.test.ts. Extract the displayed get_bazaar_tools function from the actual page and execute it using python3 through a Node child process with stdin, never a temporary file. Supply standard-library-only stubs for StructuredTool, ClientSession, and two distinct tool records. Invoke both coroutine wrappers and both synchronous wrappers outside a running loop; assert each calls its own name with its own arguments, including repeated interleaved calls. Run node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/langchain-tool-closure.test.ts. No external Python packages or network calls are required. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflow, package.json, or auth changes. work on the assigned branch you are on.
